name: Beleaguered Castle
description: Beleaguered Castle is a classic 'Open Packer' solitaire game where all 52 cards are visible from the start. The four Aces are stripped out to form the foundations (the 'Castle') in the center, and the remaining 48 cards are dealt into eight 'Wings' (side piles) of six cards each. The player must build the foundations up by suit from Ace to King, moving cards between the wings in descending sequence regardless of suit. It is a game of pure skill and deep calculation, often compared to FreeCell but without the safety net of empty transition cells.

history.origins: First recorded in 1883 in William B. Dick's American collection 'Dick's Games of Patience', and it has appeared regularly in patience compendia since then. It is an open packer castle game closely related to other layout-focused solitaires.
timeline: 1883: First recorded by William B. Dick in 'Dick's Games of Patience' in the United States.
20th century: Reprinted in multiple patience compendia, helping standardize the modern rules.
Late 20th century: Often compared with FreeCell in solitaire literature, though it remains stricter and less forgiving.
history.cultural: Often cited as one of the few solitaires where a skilled player can win nearly 100% of deals (though this is disputed for the strict rule variants).
history.evolution: The game's harsh 'no empty cell' rule led to variants like 'Streets and Alleys' (Citadel) which place the Aces in the tableau to ease the opening.

setup.players: One player (solitaire). The player acts alone: they remove the four Aces to form the foundations, deal the remaining 48 cards into eight wings, then move exposed cards between the tableau and foundations until all cards are built up or no legal moves remain.
setup.dealing: 1. Remove the 4 Aces and place them in a vertical column in the center (The Foundations). 2. Deal the remaining 48 cards face up into 8 horizontal rows (Wings) on either side of the Aces (4 rows left, 4 rows right). Each row has 6 cards overlapping so only the end card is accessible.

rules.objective: Build all four Foundation piles up from Ace to King in the same suit.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Foundations**: Build UP by suit (e.g., 2♥ on A♥). 2. **Wings (Tableau)**: The top (exposed) card of any Wing is available for play. You can build DOWN on the wings regardless of suit (e.g., playing a 6♠ on a 7♦). 3. **Moving Cards**: Only one card can be moved at a time. 4. **Empty Spaces**: If a Wing becomes empty, you can fill the space with ANY available card (usually a King is best to start a new sequence).
keyRules: Any suit can be built on any suit in the tableau (unlike Solitaire/Klondike where it must be alternating colors).
Only the top card is movable.
Empty spaces are critical—creating one is usually the primary Short-Term Goal.

strategy.basic: Prioritize digging out the 2s and 3s. Since 2s are buried, you can't build your foundations. Look for moves that uncover low cards.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Empty Slot' Gambit: Don't fill an empty wing space unless it helps you unblock another pile. An empty space is a 'virtual cell' that lets you shuttle cards around.
strategy.advanced: Reverse Building: Before moving a card to a foundation, check if you need it in the Tableau to hold a lower card. Sometimes keeping a 5 on the board allows you to stack a 4 on it, clearing space elsewhere.
tips: Don't build down a long sequence on a pile that hides a card you need immediately.

variations.name: Citadel
variations.description: Aces are not removed at the start. Instead, they are shuffled into the deck and must be played to the foundations as they become available.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Citadel is documented as a rules variant of Beleaguered Castle; engine overrides have not been modeled separately yet.

variations.name: Streets and Alleys
variations.description: Similar to Citadel, but foundations are not placed in the center; they are built above the tableau.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Streets and Alleys shares the same core engine but adjusts layout; this JSON records it as a descriptive variant without separate overrides.

scoring.description: Standard Solitaire scoring based on the number of cards moved to foundations.
scoring.winCondition: Successful placement of all 52 cards on foundations.

synthesis.shortDescription: A pure test of logic. With all cards visible from the start, there are no surprises—only mistakes. Maneuver your forces across the eight wings to free the royals and lift the siege. Harder than FreeCell, more rewarding than Klondike.
